title: Vapnik, Chervonenkis, and the Theory Behind the Support Vector Machine
explainer: The SVM classifier in scikit-learn descends from statistical learning theory developed by Vladimir Vapnik and Alexey Chervonenkis, whose work on when a model generalizes rather than memorizes dates back to the 1960s-70s, with the modern soft-margin SVM formalized by Vapnik and collaborators after he emigrated to the US in the early 1990s. The theory's central question - how much a model can fit before it stops generalizing - is exactly what you're probing every time you compare training and validation accuracy.

title: Leo Breiman and the 2001 Random Forests Paper
explainer: The RandomForestClassifier and RandomForestRegressor in scikit-learn implement an algorithm statistician Leo Breiman published in a 2001 paper called simply 'Random Forests,' which combined his own earlier bootstrap-aggregating ('bagging') idea with randomized feature selection to decorrelate individual trees. Breiman came to this corner of machine learning relatively late in a career otherwise spent in classical statistics, which is part of why the method is unusually well-grounded in variance-reduction theory rather than ad hoc tuning.
